clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man presented with worsening respiratory distress, proximal muscle weakness, hyperpigmentation, significant weight loss, and signs of superior vena cava syndrome. Chest CT on admission revealed a large lobulated soft-tissue mass (11.7×5.7×4.7 cm) at the right hilar region with severely stretched proximal superior vena cava causing luminal narrowing, confirming superior vena cava syndrome. Bronchoscopic biopsy was ordered to confirm histology, but no histopathological report text was provided. The known final diagnosis from the case states that histological examination of the bronchial biopsy confirmed small cell lung cancer. Thus, the clinical and imaging findings combined with the noted histological confirmation support the diagnosis of SCLC causing superior vena cava syndrome and related symptoms.
